tests: doctor FAILs a declared retention path when git cannot say whether it is ignored, naming git's reason, for a fleet that is no repository and for one whose config git cannot parse

consumesExternalOutput.provenance: The retention check in src/commands/doctor.ts decides whether a declared path survives a clone from the exit code of `git check-ignore -q`, so red-witness rule (f) binds this witness. The capture records, on git 2.43.0 and on the Ubuntu 22.04 git 2.34.1, exit 0 for an ignored path, exit 1 for an unignored one, and two structurally different non-answers, both exit 128: a directory that is no repository (`fatal: not a git repository ...`) and a repository whose .git/config git cannot parse (`fatal: bad config line N ...`). The named test reproduces each non-answer live against the capture in a fleet whose retention paths are on disk, then asserts doctor FAILs naming git's own line instead of printing PASS present and tracked. Member 0 folds exit 128 back into not ignored at the classifier (the pre-fix reading, which prints PASS); member 1 keeps the classifier and drops the arm that reports the non-answer, so the FAIL names the wrong reason.
